title: The uniqueness problem in private systems
excerpts: In voting and token distribution systems, each participant must be able to join exactly once.
The challenge is guaranteeing uniqueness without exposing the participant's identity.
Nullifiers solve this problem by adding an exclusion layer without revealing which citizen participated.

title: The nullifier as an exclusion witness
excerpts: A nullifier is a cryptographic value that marks an action as already performed.
It is generated from the user's secret key and a unique action identifier.
The nullifier is published to the ledger but doesn't reveal who generated it.

codeBlocks.title: Nullifier generation in a complete circuit

title: How a nullifier is generated
excerpts: The hash function takes the secret key and an event identifier.
The result is a seemingly random but deterministic value.
Only someone who knows the secret key can generate the correct nullifier.

title: The nullifier lives in the ledger
excerpts: Once generated, the nullifier is saved in the ledger as an exclusion witness.
The smart contract verifies the nullifier doesn't exist before accepting an action.
This prevents the same citizen from participating twice.

title: The double-voting problem
excerpts: In any voting system, a malicious citizen could attempt to vote multiple times.
Privacy makes it difficult to detect this attack because we don't know who the voter is.
Nullifiers solve this by allowing exclusion verification without revealing identity.

title: The nullifier as an exclusion witness
excerpts: When a citizen votes, a nullifier is generated and registered in the ledger.
The next attempt with the same citizen will find the nullifier already registered.
The system rejects the action without needing to know the identity.

title: Double-spending: the same problem
excerpts: The nullifier concept also applies to token systems.
A user shouldn't be able to spend the same token twice.
The nullifier marks the token as 'spent' after the first use.

title: Privacy is maintained
excerpts: The ledger only sees the nullifier, not the user's identity.
The contract knows that 'something has been used' but cannot link it to an identity.
This preserves privacy while maintaining system integrity.

title: Linkability: relating without revealing
excerpts: Sometimes we want to link actions from the same user without revealing who they are.
For example: verifying eligibility for multiple airdrop rounds.
Round context enables this scoped one-time control.

title: The round scopes one-time actions
excerpts: The round identifies the scope in which one action may be used.
Combined with the secret key, it produces a different nullifier for a new round.
The round scope does not by itself guarantee anonymity or unlinkability.

codeBlocks.title: Nullifier with round context

title: Formula with round context
excerpts: The nullifier uses a persistent hash over a domain separator, round bytes, and the secret key.
The same secret and same round produce the same nullifier and are rejected on replay.
The same secret with a new round produces a new scoped nullifier and is allowed.

codeBlocks.title: Round-scoped one-time action

title: Granular control of linking
excerpts: Choosing what data to include in the hash controls when there's linkability.
Same secret plus same round: the replay is rejected.
Same secret plus a new round: the action is allowed.
Hashing alone does not guarantee anonymity or unlinkability.

title: Private voting system
excerpts: Each voter generates a nullifier with their secret key.
The contract saves the nullifier in a set of 'already voted'.
The election result is public; who voted for whom remains private.

title: Airdrop distribution
excerpts: The contract verifies eligibility through ZK proofs.
Each eligible address generates a nullifier when claiming tokens.
This prevents claiming the same airdrop twice.

title: The circuit validates the nullifier
excerpts: The circuit performs two critical verifications.
First: the nullifier was generated with the correct secret key.
Second: the nullifier doesn't yet exist in the ledger set.

codeBlocks.title: Nullifier validation

title: The nullifier set is the key
excerpts: Without a public nullifier set, there's no way to prevent double-spending.
The set is your exclusion list.
Each new nullifier must be verified against the set before accepting the action.
